rows.description: A friend notices someone laughing at jokes they used to dislike or dropping old values. A private, kind check-in beats public teasing and leaves room for the person to explain.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: amusement

rows.description: A young professional stays late because everyone does, though the work is done. They fear being seen as less committed and rarely ask whether the norm actually serves anyone.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: fear

rows.description: A mature young adult sorts norms into those worth following, such as courtesy, and those to decline politely, such as gossip. They dissent calmly, without needing to win or to condemn the group.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: calm

rows.description: A toddler stops or goes on according to the caregiver's face and tone. They obey the emotional signal more than the words, which is how authority is first felt.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young child obeys quickly when an adult's voice turns sharp, to avoid disapproval. The behaviour looks like good discipline while the inner state is anxiety.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: fear, anxiety

rows.description: A child does what a teacher or elder says simply because of who said it. Trust in adults is healthy, but they may not yet separate a fair rule from an unfair order.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: trust

rows.description: A child is told by an older student or adult to hide something, pick on someone or keep a secret. They feel a pull between obedience and a stomach-sinking sense of wrongness.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
possibly related concept (heuristic): Milgram-style obedience

rows.description: A teenager begins asking why a rule exists and who made it. This is healthy developmental testing, though it can look like defiance to adults who expect quick compliance.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: hostility

rows.subtype: Teacher or coach crossing a line [Receiver]
rows.description: A student is pressured by a coach, tutor or senior to do something that feels wrong, with respect and fear mixed. They may freeze or comply because refusing an authority feels unthinkable.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: admiration, fear
possibly related concept (heuristic): Milgram-style obedience

rows.description: A teenager learns to say I understand the rule, but I do not think this is fair, and asks to discuss it. They separate respect for a person from agreement with every command.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: admiration
